He is also a [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] producer. He was an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] college player at [[Boston College Eagles basketball|Boston College]] and finished as one of the greatest players in the program's history. == Early life == Bell played high school basketball at the [[Academy of Holy Angels]] in [[Richfield, Minnesota]]. He was a 4-year letter winner, and Mr. Basketball finalist in Minnesota. In his senior season, he averaged 35.9 points, 6.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists and led the state of Minnesota in scoring. He captured the Missota Conference Player of the Year honors as a senior. In his senior season, his season high in scoring was 47 points, his season low in scoring was 24 points. He scored 45 points in a win over Minnehaha Academy (Dec. 1998). Bell served as team captain as a junior and senior. He finished his school career at Holy Angels as the career scoring leader with 2,491 points (in 97 games). In the state of Minnesota, he ranks fourth on the state's career scoring list. == College career == Bell was an [[All-American]] at [[Boston College Eagles basketball|Boston College]], winning a conference player of the year award, and sharing another with [[Troy Murphy]]. He ended his career breaking the record for most points scored in Boston College history with 2,632, breaking the record previously set by [[Dana Barros]]. He was named [[Big East Conference]] player of the year after both his sophomore (shared) and senior seasons, joining [[Troy Murphy]], [[Richard Hamilton (basketball)|Richard Hamilton]], [[Patrick Ewing]], and [[Chris Mullin (basketball)|Chris Mullin]] as the only players to win the award multiple times. On January 25, 2020, Bell's number 2 was retired by Boston College.{{cite news|title=Boston College basketball retires jersey of all-time leading scorer Troy Bell|url=https://www.wcvb.com/article/boston-college-eagles-basketball-retires-jersey-of-all-time-leading-scorer-troy-bell/|access-date=January 25, 2020|work=wcvb.com|date=January 25, 2020}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} == Professional career == === NBA === Bell was drafted 16th overall by the [[Boston Celtics]] in the first round of the [[2003 NBA draft]], but was traded on draft night to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] along with [[Dahntay Jones]] for [[Marcus Banks]] and [[Kendrick Perkins]]. He played in 6 games for the Grizzlies in 2003/04 season. On October 1, 2005, the [[New Orleans Hornets|New Orleans/Oklahoma City Hornets]] signed Bell as a [[free agent]], but October 18 they announced that they had waived him. He had played a total of 10 minutes in the Hornets' first two preseason games. Those 6 games with the Grizzlies ended up being Bell's only playing time in the NBA, as his final game was played on March 26, 2004, in a 109 - 86 win over the [[Houston Rockets]]. Bell recorded 2 points, 1 turnover and 1 foul in only 4 minutes of playing time. === NBA Development League === In 2006, Bell took up [[boxing]] while working out for the NBA.[http://wcco.com/sports/local_story_180233635.html Former MN Hoops Star Trying Out Boxing] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927004503/http://wcco.com/sports/local_story_180233635.html |date=2007-09-27 }}, June 29, 2006 He was selected as the 12th pick by the [[Albuquerque Thunderbirds]] in the first round of the 2006 [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]] draft.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/draft_2006.html NBA Development League Announces 2006 Draft Results] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070219055015/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/draft_2006.html |date=2007-02-19 }} He was signed by the [[Austin Toros]] of the D-League when [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jay Williams]] was waived due to injury in late December 2006.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/Bell_Williams_061230.html Toros Sign Troy Bell, Waive Jay Williams] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090115094645/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/Bell_Williams_061230.html |date=2009-01-15 }} === Europe === Two seasons after [[2003-04 NBA season|2003–04]], Bell played briefly in Spain ([[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]]) and in Germany ([[Frankfurt Skyliners]]). For the 2007–2008 season, he signed first for the Italian [[Serie A (basketball)|Serie A]] team, [[Pallacanestro Biella|Angelico Biella]], then on 12 March 2008 moved to [[Fastweb Casale Monferrato]].[http://www.legaduebasket.it/player/?id=BEL-TRO-80 LegaDue Basket: Troy Bell]. He played the 2008–2009 and 2009–2010 seasons with [[Gruppo Triboldi Basket]], also known for sponsorship reasons as Vanoli Soresina or Vanoli Cremona, in Serie A, the top level of Italian basketball. In August 2010 he signed with [[Entente Orléanaise]] in [[France]].[https://thehoopsmarket.blogspot.com/2010/08/orleans-inks-troy-bell.html Orleans inks Troy Bell] In the spring of 2011, Bell played with [[Pallacanestro Reggiana|Trenkwalder Reggio Emilia]]. In 2012, he signed with Pallacanestro Sant'Antimo, a second league club in Italy. In late February 2013, Bell rejoined Trenkwalder Reggio Emilia. The contract was signed for the end of the 2012–13 season with an option for 2013–14.[http://web.legabasket.it/news/?id=113083 Trenkwalder, ecco Troy Bell: 'Felice di tornare, lavorero' duro per entrare subito in sintonia con la squadra'] === Argentina === On December 24, 2015, Bell signed with [[San Lorenzo de Almagro (basketball)|San Lorenzo]] of [[Liga Nacional de Básquet|Argentina]].{{cite web|url=http://www.latinbasket.com/Argentina/news/432428/San-Lorenzo-tabs-Troy-Bell,-ex-Akhisar-Bld|title=San Lorenzo tabs Troy Bell, ex Akhisar Bld|work=Latinbasket.com|date=December 24, 2015|access-date=December 25, 2015}} ==See also== * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball career free throw scoring leaders]] * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball career scoring leaders]] ==References== {{reflist}} == External links == * [https://web.archive.org/web/20060712101057/http://www.sportsstats.com/jazzyj/greats/03/bell.htm College stats] @ sportsstats.com * {{basketballstats|bbr=b/belltr01|name=Troy Bell}} {{navboxes|list= {{2003 NBA draft}} {{2001 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{2003 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{Pallacanestro Reggiana 2013–14 EuroChallenge champions}} }} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Bell, Troy}} [[Category:1980 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:A.S.
